html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Explain observability and the three signals: metrics, logs and traces
  • Describe OpenTelemetry, Prometheus and Alertmanager
  • Define SLI, SLO, SLA and error budget
  • Name the Kubernetes signals, and the basics of FinOps and OpenCost

2Monitoring versus observability, metrics, logs and traces, the Kubernetes signals

Running case

Harbor Books Wants to See Checkout

  • Checkout feels slow for some customers, and the team needs metrics, logs and traces for the orders service
  • Management wants a latency target for checkout, and a clear view of how often it is missed
  • Finance wants to understand the monthly cloud bill for the shop
  • In this module you learn how to see the system, and what it costs

Monitoring, Observability and the Three Signals

  • Observability is understanding a system's internal state from its outputs; it lets you ask new questions, even about unknown unknowns
  • Monitoring watches known signals and alerts when they go wrong
  • Metrics: numbers aggregated over time, such as error rate, CPU use and request rate
  • Logs: timestamped messages; traces: the path of one request through services, made of spans
  • Code must be instrumented to emit these signals

Exam tip

Metrics tell you that, logs tell you what, traces tell you where.

Kubernetes Signals

Signal Source What it tells you
Resource metrics Metrics Server CPU and memory of Pods and nodes, for autoscaling and kubectl top; not a monitoring system
Object state kube-state-metrics metrics about the state of objects, not the health of the components
Events the API what happened to an object: kubectl get events
Audit log the API server who did what through the API
Logs containers, kubelet, control plane what the components printed
Exam tip

Metrics Server for autoscaling; kube-state-metrics for object state.

3OpenTelemetry, API, SDK and Collector

OpenTelemetry: API, SDK and Collector

  • OpenTelemetry (OTel) is an open source, vendor-neutral framework to generate, export and collect traces, metrics and logs
  • It is not a backend: storing and showing the data is left to tools such as Prometheus and Jaeger
  • The API and the SDK (software development kit) instrument code; OTLP is the standard protocol; semantic conventions name common data
  • The Collector receives, processes and exports data, so a service can hand it off quickly
  • It grew out of OpenTracing and OpenCensus

Exam tip

OpenTelemetry produces telemetry; it does not store it.

4Prometheus, exporters, PromQL, metric types, Alertmanager, Grafana, Fluent Bit, Fluentd, Jaeger

Prometheus: Pull, Exporters and PromQL Archived topic

  • Prometheus is an open-source monitoring and alerting toolkit that keeps metrics as time series with labels
  • It pulls (scrapes) metrics over HTTP from targets; a Pushgateway serves short-lived jobs
  • Exporters expose metrics for services that have none; targets come from service discovery
  • PromQL queries the time series
  • Metric types: counter (only goes up), gauge (up and down), histogram (buckets), summary (quantiles)

Exam tip

Prometheus pulls; a counter only goes up.

Alerting and the Tool Landscape

Tool Role
Alertmanager takes alerts from Prometheus, then deduplicates, groups and routes them to receivers such as email or PagerDuty
Grafana dashboards: queries and visualizes metrics wherever they are stored
Fluent Bit a lightweight agent that collects, processes and forwards logs, metrics and traces
Fluentd an open-source log collector that unifies logging
Jaeger a distributed tracing platform
  • Prometheus decides that an alert fires; Alertmanager decides who hears about it
Exam tip

Alertmanager routes alerts; Grafana draws dashboards.

5SLI, SLO, SLA and error budgets

SLI, SLO, SLA and Error Budgets

  • SLI: a measurement of a service's behavior, ideally from the user's point of view
  • SLO: the target for an SLI; it is how reliability is communicated
  • SLA: a contract with users, with consequences if the SLOs are missed
  • Error budget: 100% minus the SLO: the unreliability you may spend; when it is used up, put stability first
  • 100% is the wrong target

Exam tip

SLI measures, SLO targets, SLA promises.

6Cost management, FinOps and OpenCost

Cost Management and FinOps Archived topic

Term Meaning
FinOps an operational framework and cultural practice: engineering, finance and business share accountability for technology spend
OpenCost an open source project that shows what Kubernetes and cloud resources cost, now and over time, and how the spend is allocated across applications and teams
  • Requests and limits (Module 4) and autoscaling (Module 5) shape what a workload reserves, and so what it costs
  • Cost needs the same visibility as reliability: measure first, then decide
Exam tip

FinOps is a practice; OpenCost is a tool for seeing spend.

7Exam Q&A

7.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Which signal shows the path of a single request through several services?

  • AMetrics, which are numbers aggregated over a period of time
  • BTraces, which are made of spans that follow a request across services
  • CLogs, which are timestamped messages written by one service at a time
  • DEvents, which are the changes that Kubernetes records for an object
Show the answer

Answer: B. A distributed trace follows one request as it propagates through services, and is built from spans. Metrics aggregate numbers, logs are messages, and Kubernetes events describe changes to objects.

S2What does OpenTelemetry provide, and what does it leave to other tools?

  • AIt stores all metrics itself and leaves only the instrumentation of the code to other tools
  • BIt builds dashboards and alert rules, and leaves the generation of telemetry to the application
  • CIt replaces Prometheus and Jaeger, and leaves the Collector to the cloud provider that hosts the cluster
  • DIt generates, exports and collects telemetry, and leaves storage and visualization to other tools
Show the answer

Answer: D. OpenTelemetry is a vendor-neutral framework for generating, exporting and collecting traces, metrics and logs. It is not a backend, so storage and visualization are left to tools such as Prometheus, Jaeger and Grafana.

S3How does Prometheus normally collect metrics?

  • AIt pulls, or scrapes, them over HTTP from targets such as applications and exporters
  • BEach application pushes its metrics to the server whenever a request arrives
  • CThe Alertmanager gathers them from the nodes and passes them to the server
  • DThe kubelet writes them into etcd, and the server reads them from there later
Show the answer

Answer: A. Prometheus uses a pull model: it scrapes metrics over HTTP from its targets. Pushing is supported only through an intermediary gateway for short-lived jobs, and the Alertmanager only handles alerts.

S4Harbor Books measures how long checkout takes, and then sets a target for that measurement. What are the two called?

  • AAn SLA for the measurement, and an SLI for the target
  • BAn error budget for the measurement, and an SLO for the target
  • CAn SLI for the measurement, and an SLO for the target
  • DAn SLO for the measurement, and an SLA for the target
Show the answer

Answer: C. An SLI is a measurement of a service's behavior, and an SLO is the target for it. An SLA is a contract with consequences if the objectives are missed, and the error budget is 100% minus the SLO.

S5What does OpenCost provide?

  • AAutomatic scaling of Pods when the monthly cloud bill grows too large
  • BVisibility into what Kubernetes and cloud resources cost, now and over time, and how that spend is split
  • CEncryption of Secrets and of the data of Persistent Volumes in the cluster
  • DA query language for the metrics that the Prometheus server stores as time series
Show the answer

Answer: B. OpenCost shows teams what Kubernetes and cloud resources cost, and how spend is allocated across applications and teams. It does not scale Pods, encrypt data or query metrics.
